In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NF2 is caused by a germline mutation in one allele, with a second somatic mutation in the other allele, and that sporadic schwannomas are caused by two somatic mutations in the merlin gene.
NF2 is a disease caused by mutations in the NF2 gene.
the merlin tumor suppressor is a key player in the pathogenesis of both NF2 and sporadic schwannomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NF2 gene is a candidate tumor suppressor gene that is inactivated by mutations that result in the production of a truncated protein.
we have identified 32 different mutations in the NF2 gene, which is consistent with the notion that this gene has been mutated in schwannomas.
the merlin protein, which is a component of a family of proteins that are involved in the organization of the cytoskeleton, is a major target for mutation in the development of schwannomas.

we have developed the first set of assays for scanning for merlin mutations.
